```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  paste0(
    "\n\n<details>\n<summary>",
    options$summary,
    "</summary>\n\n",
    source_hook(x, options),
    "\n\n</details>\n\n"
  )
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(summary = "Show R code", message = FALSE)
```

## Example data

Highcharts reads each row as a point. The series type determines which
fields it uses. A line reads a position (`x`) and a measurement (`y`).
A range reads `low` and `high`. A bubble adds `z` for size, and a
Sankey link takes `from`, `to` and `weight`. The `name` field labels a point.

With these column names you can call `hchart(temperatures, "columnrange")`
directly. If your columns are called `minimum` and `maximum`, map them
with `hcaes(low = minimum, high = maximum)`. The four small tables below
are reused throughout the gallery.

```{r common-data, summary="Show the four example datasets"}
library(highcharter)
library(dplyr)
hc_set_theme(
  "hcrt",
  colors = c("#508CC8", "#61BC7B", "#F49952", "#9C9EDB", "#6699A1")
)

# Daily mean, minimum and maximum temperature (°C).
# fmt: skip
temperatures <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name, ~y, ~low, ~high,
  "Mon", 15,   12,    18,
  "Tue", 17,   13,    21,
  "Wed", 14,   11,    17,
  "Thu", 16,   12,    20,
  "Fri", 18,   14,    22
)

# Visitors by last stage reached (y) and typical time at that stage in minutes (z).
stages <- tibble(
  name = c("Visit", "Start", "Review", "Submit"),
  y = c(35, 12, 8, 25),
  z = c(1, 4, 3, 2)
)

# People assigned to each team and subteam.
# fmt: skip
teams <- tibble::tribble(
  ~from,     ~to,       ~weight,
  "Studio",  "Design",       12,
  "Studio",  "Build",        18,
  "Design",  "Web",           7,
  "Design",  "Print",         5,
  "Build",   "Apps",         18
)

# Coordinates (degrees), approximate elevation (m) and illustrative wind (m/s, degrees).
# fmt: skip
capitals <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,           ~lon,   ~lat, ~z, ~speed, ~direction,
  "Santiago",    -70.67, -33.45, 520,     5,        210,
  "Lima",        -77.04, -12.05, 150,     8,        180,
  "Brasília",    -47.88, -15.79, 1170,    3,         90,
  "Buenos Aires",-58.38, -34.60,  25,    11,        135
)
```

```{r gallery-layout, summary="Show the gallery layout code"}
gallery <- function(types, draw) {
  charts <- lapply(types, function(type) {
    draw(type) |>
      hc_title(text = type, style = list(fontSize = "16px")) |>
      hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>
      hc_tooltip(outside = TRUE) |>
      hc_size(height = 235)
  })
  htmltools::div(class = "chart-grid", charts)
}
```

## Measurements and ranges

Line and column charts read the daily mean from `y`. Range charts use
`low` and `high`. The same five rows work on a polar axis.

```{r temperature-example, eval=FALSE}
hchart(temperatures, "columnrange", colorByPoint = TRUE) |>
  hc_xAxis(type = "category")
```

```{r temperature-gallery, summary="Show all temperature charts in R"}
gallery(
  c(
    "line",
    "spline",
    "area",
    "areaspline",
    "column",
    "arearange",
    "areasplinerange",
    "columnrange",
    "errorbar",
    "dumbbell",
    "polar line",
    "polar column",
    "polar columnrange"
  ),
  function(label) {
    type <- sub("^polar ", "", label)
    hchart(
      temperatures,
      type,
      name = "Temperature",
      colorByPoint = TRUE,
      lineColor = "#508CC8",
      fillColor = "#508CC866",
      tooltip = list(valueSuffix = " °C")
    ) |>
      hc_chart(type = type, polar = startsWith(label, "polar")) |>
      hc_xAxis(categories = temperatures$name)
  }
)
```

## Quantities by category

The four counts add up to 80 visitors. A pie shows the stage at which each
visitor stopped. For a funnel, sum from the last stage backwards to count
everyone who reached each stage. Variable-width columns and variable-radius
pie slices also show the typical time spent at each stage (`z`).

```{r stages-example, eval=FALSE}
hchart(stages, "pie", colorByPoint = TRUE)
```

```{r stages-gallery, summary="Show all stage charts in R"}
gallery(
  c(
    "bar",
    "column",
    "columnpyramid",
    "pie",
    "lollipop",
    "dotplot",
    "item",
    "waterfall",
    "variwide",
    "variablepie",
    "timeline",
    "packedbubble",
    "treemap",
    "wordcloud",
    "funnel",
    "pyramid",
    "cylinder",
    "funnel3d",
    "pyramid3d"
  ),
  function(type) {
    points <- stages
    if (type %in% c("funnel", "pyramid", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d")) {
      points$y <- rev(cumsum(rev(points$y)))
    }
    if (type %in% c("packedbubble", "treemap")) {
      points$value <- points$y
    }
    if (type == "timeline") {
      points$x <- seq_len(nrow(points)) - 1L
      points$label <- points$name
    }
    if (type == "wordcloud") {
      points$weight <- points$y
    }
    hchart(points, type, name = "Visitors", colorByPoint = TRUE) |>
      hc_xAxis(categories = stages$name) |>
      hc_chart(
        type = type,
        options3d = list(
          enabled = type %in% c("cylinder", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d"),
          alpha = 12,
          beta = 15
        )
      )
  }
)
```

## Relationships and hierarchies

Each link runs from a parent team to a subteam. Its weight is the number
of people in the subteam. Compare how the same organization looks when
the chart emphasizes the flow, the connections or the hierarchy.

```{r teams-example, eval=FALSE}
hchart(teams, "sankey")
```

```{r teams-gallery, summary="Show all team charts in R"}
gallery(
  c(
    "sankey",
    "dependencywheel",
    "arcdiagram",
    "networkgraph",
    "organization",
    "treegraph",
    "sunburst"
  ),
  function(type) {
    if (type %in% c("treegraph", "sunburst")) {
      nodes <- bind_rows(
        tibble(id = "Studio", name = "Studio"),
        transmute(teams, id = to, parent = from, name = to, value = weight)
      )
      return(hchart(nodes, type))
    }
    hchart(teams, type) |> hc_chart(inverted = type == "organization")
  }
)
```

### Style network nodes and tooltips

The same links can carry node-level labels. Use each subteam’s headcount
to size its marker and show the count on hover.

```{r mapping-networkgraph}
headcounts <- c(
  Studio = sum(teams$weight[teams$from == "Studio"]),
  setNames(teams$weight, teams$to)
)
nodes <- lapply(names(headcounts), function(id) {
  n <- headcounts[[id]]
  list(id = id, marker = list(radius = 3 * sqrt(n)), custom = list(people = n))
})
hchart(
  teams,
  "networkgraph",
  nodes = nodes,
  dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "{point.name}", linkFormat = ""),
  tooltip = list(
    headerFormat = "",
    nodeFormat = "{point.name}: {point.custom.people} people"
  )
)
```

## Positions, bubbles and wind

Longitude and latitude locate each capital. Bubble size and the third
scatter axis represent elevation. Vector length shows wind speed and its
angle shows direction. Wind barbs compare the same winds by city.

```{r capitals-example}
positions <- capitals |> rename(x = lon, y = lat)
```

```{r capitals-gallery, summary="Show all capital charts in R"}
gallery(
  c("scatter", "bubble", "scatter3d", "vector", "windbarb", "polygon"),
  function(type) {
    if (type == "windbarb") {
      return(
        hchart(capitals, type, hcaes(value = speed), color = "#508CC8") |>
          hc_xAxis(categories = capitals$name)
      )
    }
    points <- positions
    if (type == "polygon") {
      points <- points[chull(points$x, points$y), ]
    }
    if (type == "vector") {
      points$length <- points$speed
    }
    hchart(points, type, name = "Capitals") |>
      hc_chart(
        type = type,
        options3d = list(
          enabled = type == "scatter3d",
          alpha = 15,
          beta = 20
        )
      ) |>
      hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Longitude")) |>
      hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Latitude"))
  }
)
```

The polygon outlines the four locations. To place the bubbles on a map,
reuse their longitude, latitude and elevation with a South America basemap.

```{r capitals-map}
map_file <- here::here(
  "dev",
  "examples-charts",
  "data",
  "maps",
  "custom-south-america.geo.json"
)
hcmap(
  jsonlite::read_json(map_file),
  nullColor = "#D9E3E8",
  showInLegend = FALSE
) |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "mapbubble",
    data = list_parse(capitals),
    name = "Elevation",
    minSize = 6,
    maxSize = "10%",
    tooltip = list(pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.z} m")
  )
```

## Other point formats

A two-dimensional grid supplies one value per cell for heatmaps, tilemaps
and contours. The detailed tile map and vector field follow below.

```{r grid-data}
cells <- expand.grid(x = 0:5, y = 0:5) |> mutate(value = sin(x) + cos(y))
```

```{r grid-types}
gallery(c("heatmap", "tilemap", "contour"), function(type) {
  hchart(cells, type) |> hc_colorAxis(min = -2, max = 2)
})
```

### Comparing a measurement with a target

The bullet marks an illustrative target of 18 °C against each daily mean.

```{r temperature-target}
hchart(temperatures, "bullet", hcaes(target = 18), colorByPoint = TRUE) |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = temperatures$name)
```

### A streamgraph with multiple series

Each band is a spending category in the built-in US personal expenditure
table. Band thickness shows expenditure in billions of dollars.

```{r spending-streamgraph}
spending <- as.data.frame(
  as.table(USPersonalExpenditure),
  responseName = "amount"
)
hchart(
  spending,
  "streamgraph",
  hcaes(x = as.integer(as.character(Var2)), y = amount, group = Var1)
) |>
  hc_yAxis(visible = FALSE)
```

## Task intervals

Each row spans two dates. Map the start to `x`, the end to `x2` and the lane's zero-based index to `y`.

```{r mapping-xrange}
tasks <- data.frame(
  start = base::as.Date(c("2025-01-06", "2025-01-08")),
  finish = base::as.Date(c("2025-01-09", "2025-01-13")),
  lane = 0:1
)
hchart(tasks, "xrange", hcaes(x = start, x2 = finish, y = lane)) |>
  hc_yAxis(categories = c("Design", "Review"))
```

## Specialized chart recipes

Some charts need their own data shape. These examples include weighted arcs,
unit symbols, tile maps and vector fields, with the R code beside each result.

```{r specialized-recipes, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
recipes <- c(
  "arcdiagram",
  "item",
  "wordcloud",
  "tilemap",
  "vector",
  "venn",
  "solidgauge"
)
for (name in recipes) {
  path <- here::here("dev", "examples-charts", paste0(name, ".R"))
  cat(knitr::spin_child(path), sep = "\n")
}
```

## Markers and tooltips

See [Icons and pictograms](icons-and-pictograms.html) for image markers,
icons in tooltips and symbols that represent individual items.

The [Maps](maps.html) and [Stock](stock.html) articles cover geographic
and financial series. The [bundle gallery](../bundle-gallery.html) has an
example for every registered series type.

## Distributions

For a histogram in R, pass the result of `hist(..., plot = FALSE)` to
`hchart()`. See the [precomputed histogram example](hchart.html#precomputed-histograms).

### Box plot

Each row supplies the two whisker ends, the lower and upper quartiles, and the median for one box.

```{r mapping-boxplot}
waits <- data.frame(
  clinic = c("North", "South"),
  lower = c(4, 6),
  p25 = c(6, 8),
  p50 = c(10, 12),
  p75 = c(14, 15),
  upper = c(19, 22)
)
hchart(
  waits,
  "boxplot",
  hcaes(x = clinic, low = lower, q1 = p25, median = p50, q3 = p75, high = upper)
)
```

### Normal curve

The `bellcurve` series fits a normal curve using the sample mean and standard
deviation. For a kernel density estimate, see [Densities](hchart.html#densities).

```{r bellcurve}
highchart() |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "scatter",
    id = "scores",
    data = c(52, 58, 61, 63, 65, 67, 74),
    visible = FALSE,
    showInLegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "bellcurve",
    baseSeries = "scores",
    name = "Normal curve"
  )
```
